body.statement:
Assume \(L_r>0\), and define
\[
 d_{\max}=\begin{cases}
 L_r,&L_r\le M,\\
 2M-M^2/L_r,&L_r>M.
 \end{cases}
\]
For \(0<d<d_{\max}\), let
\[
 x(d)=\begin{cases}
 \sqrt{d/L_r},&d\le M^2/L_r,\\
 \{d+M^2/L_r\}/(2M),&d>M^2/L_r,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad a(d)=1-x(d).
\]
Select the intensity-optimized clipped-ramp pair with start \(a(d)\), and write
\[
 \gamma_n=\max_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\tau_n^\sigma\notin D_n\}.
\]
If this selected pair satisfies \(\limsup_{n\to\infty}\gamma_n\le\alpha\), then, under each sign,
\[
 \liminf_{n\to\infty}
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 \ge
 \left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This envelope is jointly optimal among deterministic late-void two-sign witnesses of the stated form with intensity profile in \(\mathcal Q\), residual magnitude bounded by \(M\), and residual Lipschitz modulus at most \(L_r\). For each selected two-sign pair, the exact randomized allocation attains the displayed asymptotic bound, but no globally attaining procedure over the full structured class is asserted.

The residual clipping elbow is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\) and is interior precisely when \(L_r>M\). If \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity profile has the additional elbow
\[
 d_q=d\!\left(1-\frac{c}{2L_q}\right).
\]
When both elbows are interior, either strict ordering \(d_q<d_r\) or \(d_r<d_q\) is possible under the declared parameter restrictions.
body.proof_tex:
The constant-intensity optimized theorem proves that \(d(x)\) is continuous and strictly increasing on \([0,1]\), has endpoint value \(d_{\max}\), and satisfies
\[
 d(x(d))=d,\qquad x(d)\in(0,1),qquad a(d)=1-x(d)\in(0,1).
\]
Fix \(d\) and the stated intensity-optimized pair. Its sharp finite-sample theorem gives
\[
 \Delta_n\ge d(x(d))=d,
 \qquad
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge\Delta_n\}
 \ge[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+,
\]
and
\[
 \eta_n^\star\longrightarrow
 \exp\{-H(a(d))\}=\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}.
\]
The event at threshold \(\Delta_n\) is contained in the event at threshold \(d\). Since the positive-part map is continuous and nondecreasing, the premise \(\limsup_n\gamma_n\le\alpha\) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \liminf_n\Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 &\ge\liminf_n[\eta_n^\star-2\gamma_n]_+\\
 &\ge\left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
 \end{aligned}
\]

For the optimization certificate, consider any two-sign late-void residual \(\widetilde r^+=g\), \(\widetilde r^-=-g\) that vanishes on \([0,a']\), is bounded in magnitude by \(M\), and is \(L_r\)-Lipschitz. Since \(g(a')=0\),
\[
 |g(u)|\le\min\{L_r(u-a')_+,M\}.
\]
Thus its limiting causal separation is at most \(d(1-a')\). To attain separation at least \(d\), strict monotonicity forces
\[
 1-a'\ge x(d),\qquad a'\le a(d).
\]
For any \(q'\in\mathcal Q\), the intensity-properties proposition gives \(q'(u)\ge q_\star(u)\) and hence a finite late-void product no larger than the \(q_\star\) product at the same start. Under \(q_\star\), the limiting void mass at start \(a'\) is \(\exp\{-H(a')\}\). Because the integrand \(q_\star(u)/u\) is positive and \(a'\le a(d)\),
\[
 H(a')\ge H(a(d)),
 \qquad
 \exp\{-H(a')\}\le\exp\{-H(a(d))\}.
\]
The clipped residual at \(a(d)\) and the pointwise-minimal intensity \(q_\star\) attain equality in both comparisons. This is the announced joint late-void optimality certificate.

The exact randomized allocation in the sharp theorem has maximum miscoverage at most \(\alpha\) for every \(n\), and its only positive-diameter output is the two-target set, whose diameter \(\Delta_n\) is at least \(d\). Hence
\[
 \Pr_\sigma\{\operatorname{diam}(D_n)\ge d\}
 =[\eta_n^\star-2\alpha]_+
 \longrightarrow
 \left[\exp\{-H(1-x(d))\}-2\alpha\right]_+.
\]
This rule uses knowledge of the selected pair and therefore proves pairwise, not global, attainment.

The residual calculation gives its interior kink at \(x_r=M/L_r\), whose image is \(d_r=M^2/L_r\); one has \(x_r\in(0,1)\) exactly when \(L_r>M\). When \(L_q>c/2\), the intensity kink is at \(u_q=c/(2L_q)\), hence at \(x_q=1-u_q\) on the diameter scale and at \(d_q=d(x_q)\). If both kinks are interior, then \(x_r\in(0,1)\), while as \(L_q\) ranges over \((c/2,\infty)\), \(x_q=1-c/(2L_q)\) ranges over \((0,1)\). Choosing \(x_q<x_r\) or \(x_q>x_r\), and using strict monotonicity of \(d\), gives respectively \(d_q<d_r\) or \(d_q>d_r\). Thus no ordering is forced by the primitive restrictions.
body.justification: Pointwise minimality of \(q_\star\) and pointwise maximality of the clipped residual jointly certify the strongest late-void envelope in the declared deterministic witness geometry.
body.gap: The intensity lower envelope introduces a second kink that the retained constant-intensity frontier cannot reveal; arbitrary finite propensity caps prevent an all-\(n\) structured-class membership claim for the new family.
body.consumer: Under honesty for a selected intensity-optimized pair, designers can compute the joint probability--diameter obstruction and locate both elbows without treating it as a global minimax guarantee.
